OPERATIVE REFERENCE

CONTROL THE ENCOUNTER.

North is up. Escape rather than eliminate. All supplies are optional; the elevator is the only required destination. Menus and Codec pause the mission.

Read before moving.The radar is north-up. White is you; coral dots are patrols. Cones stop at cover. Suspicion gives a brief chance to step back. Radar is unavailable during alert, evasion, or chaff.

Break contact.After losing sight of you, the alert counts down for eight seconds, then evasion lasts twelve. A fresh sighting restarts pursuit. The south water is a safe escape, reached from the western steps or by diving from an edge.

Make them turn around.Knock against a wall to lure a patrol, then take the opposite route. Running through puddles makes noise. Wet footsteps leave a short-lived trail that guards can investigate.

Use the box carefully.Acquire the southeast field kit. Stay still before a guard looks your way. Moving in sight, a very close inspection, or hiding after discovery defeats the disguise. Your ration auto-recovery is off while the box is worn.

Get hands-on.Approach a guard from behind with no weapon selected, then ACT to restrain. Move to drag. KNOCK throws the captive nonlethally; four STRIKE presses are lethal. ACT releases. Knockouts are temporary.

Know your tools.Stun grenades incapacitate nearby guards but can stun you too. Chaff disables the added camera and your radar for ten seconds. The northwest manifest grants a suppressor. Observation is for scouting, not first-person shooting.

Gamepad names follow the standard browser mapping (Xbox labels / physical positions). Controller support depends on the browser exposing the pad. Touch play works in portrait; landscape gives a wider tactical view.

BLACK TIDE · CARGO DOCKGenerated: 2026-09-29Model: GPT-6 Astra Pro

A standalone, offline tactical-stealth level inspired by Metal Gear Solid for the original PlayStation. The slice begins at the submerged cargo dock and ends with the freight elevator ascending toward the surface. The harbour layout, infiltration tools, radar grammar, and patrol-and-evasion rhythm provide the source connection; the title, dialogue, models, sound, and implementation are new.

Important technical and asset deviations. This delivery does not use the requested three.js 0.186.0, Rapier 0.20.0, or Vite stack. The build environment could not retrieve those packages or the requested source-game audio. It instead includes a custom native WebGPU renderer with a native WebGL2 fallback, a TypeScript engine, fixed-step custom kinematics, and 53 original synthesized MP3 assets. It is a playable self-contained alternative, not a claim that the specified stack or source-audio requirements were satisfied. The full implications are recorded below.

Launch and save

Save this HTML file and open it directly in a current browser with WebGPU or WebGL2 enabled. No server, package installation, network connection, or separate assets are required. Press Begin Infiltration. Audio unlocks on the first key press or tap. Fullscreen is available from Options or the radar toolbar; browser policy may require a direct button click. On mobile, open the HTML in an actual browser rather than a file-preview application.

Settings, the latest checkpoint, and the best result are stored in this browser's local storage when available. A checkpoint is written about every five mission seconds, on pause, and on exit. Continue Infiltration restores the current dock, inventory, patrols, lift, alert state, and statistics. Death allows checkpoint retry or a fresh insertion. Finishing removes the active checkpoint and preserves the best score. Renaming or moving a local HTML file may change its storage origin. Private browsing or restrictive file policies may disable persistence; the running level remains playable.

Try the new details

Select Explore Service Bay on the title screen. This optional start places you beside the desk with a suppressed SOCOM and extra ammunition. The same dock objective remains active. It does not write a best score. It does replace the current checkpoint, as a new run does.

For precise shots, hold V and move the mouse, then click. Gamepad: D-pad right, right stick, and RT. Touch: LOOK, joystick, and FIRE. First-person view locks movement. In the normal view, point at a prop to see its target label. Press E / A / ACT beside the door, valves, fan switch, or shift note. Hold the walk control when using the door.

Environment implementation and limits

The new system uses the existing custom engine, not Rapier. Props have simple spherical colliders, mass-weighted collision impulses, gravity, friction, damping, and sleep states. The table is a spring model. The door is an angular spring with player clearance. Both use the fixed 60 Hz simulation and interpolated rendering. This is not a general-purpose rigid-body solver. Balanced permits 24 active main props; High permits 40. Temporary shards and atmospheric particles have separate finite limits.

Damage, prop positions, valve state, spills, door state, light state, and terminal state are included in checkpoint data. Old checkpoints load with intact new details. Glass fracture uses a procedural radial pattern, not a stress simulation. Fruit uses a spherical collider, not deformation. Small debris clears after its lifetime; floor evidence remains. Guard contact can move floor props. Loose props do not block the operative or prevent extraction.

Atmospheric particles can be reduced in Options. Gameplay steam remains visible at both settings. Broken lights affect only the nearby sight-range calculation, not the whole guard state. Quiet door use reduces sound radius, not hinge speed. Audio is positional stereo with smooth gain changes, not full acoustic propagation or occlusion.

Additions, kept separate from source content

Optional field kit

A southeast maintenance cache provides a SOCOM with 12 loaded and 24 reserve rounds, a cardboard box, two stun grenades, and two chaff grenades. These are representative series tools relocated into the dock for this demo; they were not the original dock's pickups. No weapon or grenade is required for completion.

Manifest and suppressor

A northwest shipping manifest is an optional objective worth 1,200 points. It installs a suppressor and adds ammunition. One rotating camera guards this alcove: it detects, can be shot out, and is jammed by chaff. That camera and cache are additions, not claims about the source dock.

Modern information and controls

A brief suspicion ramp, explicit lift ETA, contextual interactions, adaptive touch controls, standard gamepad support, conventional movement/aim controls, optional world cones, and clearer pickup feedback improve readability without making combat mandatory. First-person view now supports precise pistol fire. Movement stays locked during observation, so aiming remains a tactical decision.

Replay and evidence

Wet footprints adapt the series' track-following idea to harbour puddles. Local checkpoints, automatic performance scaling, a score, three ranks, and best-run persistence support replay. Reinforcements and camera rules are custom interpretations, not extracted original AI routines.

Systems and encounter rules

Guard AI uses patrol, investigation, search, pursuit, captive, knockout, and dead states. Line of sight is tested against cover. Footstep splashes, wall knocks, firearm reports, and visible wet footprints can redirect patrols. A stationary cardboard box can avoid detection only before a guard has clearly discovered the operative; movement and close inspection compromise it. Shooting uses cover-occluded hitscan. The pistol reloads from a finite reserve, and quick holster/draw preserves ammunition accounting. The optional suppressor reduces its audible radius.

Stun and chaff devices follow fixed-step ballistic trajectories, collide with floor and obstacles, bounce with damping, and detonate on a fuse. Stun affects nearby line-of-sight targets, including the player; chaff blinds the added camera and the player's radar for ten seconds. Grenades are removed on detonation. Particle, footprint, reinforcement, and body counts are bounded. Equipped rations support emergency recovery; box use occupies the item slot and suppresses auto-recovery. Equipment and Codec screens pause the simulation.

Rank is GHOST for zero alerts and zero kills, FOX for at most two of each, or HOUND otherwise. Score = max(0, 10,000 − 1,150 × alerts − 550 × kills − 125 × rations used − 4 × whole mission seconds + 1,200 for the manifest). Knockouts are intentionally not penalized. The rank and score are original demo rules.

Intentionally outside the slice

The playable heliport, tank hangar, vents beyond the dock, snowfield, keycard progression, hostages, campaign inventory, bosses, boss rewards, torture sequence, story endings, and later weapon families are not included. There are no dock quests or upgrades falsely attributed to the original level; the optional manifest and suppressor are identified additions. Cigarettes, binocular inventory, body disposal beyond dragging a live captive, swimming combat, and the full cinematic presentation are not implemented. This is one complete extraction level, not the full game.

Rendering, physics, and performance

Both native backends render the same untextured, faceted world and use corresponding PBR-style GGX shader math, six local lights, soft directional shadows, analytic environment fill, contact-darkening geometry, distance fog, a high-dynamic-range scene target when supported, ACES-style tone mapping, and 4× multisample anti-aliasing. Optional restrained bloom and grain are off by default. The environment is analytic lighting, not an imported HDR panorama; contact shading is not a screen-space ambient-occlusion pass.

Auto starts conservatively and examines the 85th percentile of recent frame times. It reduces render resolution when overloaded and increases it when there is headroom; sustained low frame time can select High. High uses up to 1.5× device pixel ratio, 2,048-pixel shadows, 220 particles, and 16 active devices. Balanced uses up to 1× resolution, 1,024-pixel shadows, 100 particles, and eight active devices. Bloom sampling strength and atmospheric detail also scale. The diagnostic line reports active backend, preset, smoothed frame time, and resolution scale. Device names are not used to choose Auto quality.

Movement, enemy simulation, and grenade integration run at a fixed 60 Hz with a bounded accumulator. Actor rendering interpolates between simulation positions. Player/guard collision is custom swept substepping against simple boxes; grenade response uses gravity, damped bounce, and friction rather than a rigid-body solver. The environment is static and has no movable crate simulation. These are intentional custom-physics deviations, not Rapier bodies, plausible mass calculations, or a claim of Rapier compliance.

Checkpoint serialization — PASS, with a storage limitation. A JSON round-trip test verified equipment, player and patrol state, search phase, active grenades, wet footprints, enemy search evidence, and statistics. Browser-local persistence itself could not be verified in this sandbox's restricted page origin. The game checks storage availability and reports when saving is unavailable.

Not verified: native WebGPU rendering, actual local-file launch under the target browser, hardware gamepad and vibration, fullscreen permissions, hardware audio output, physical mobile gestures, and steady performance on Galaxy S24 / RTX 3060. This environment's administrator URL policy blocked direct file navigation, so testing used the unchanged HTML through an offline browser-page injection. Native WebGPU was not exposed in that test context; the fallback WebGL2 path was the tested renderer. These limitations are not represented as passes.

The custom backend and original audio are the principal specification deviations. Native WebGPU availability depends on the browser, graphics driver, secure-context policy, and local-file handling; initialization falls back to WebGL2. Fullscreen, audio unlock, vibration, gamepads, and local-file storage remain subject to browser permission and platform support. No claim is made that this software-rendered validation proves a steady frame rate on Galaxy S24 or RTX 3060 hardware.

First-person leaning is a modest positional shift, not the original game's complete corner-camera logic. The orthographic camera can temporarily obscure an actor behind tall cover; radar and observation are the intended scouting aids. Desktop pointer aim now selects nearby prop centers, then resolves a three-dimensional shot against intervening objects. Soft mist is sorted back to front. Multiple overlapping glass sheets still use a simple alpha blend. Source-equivalent frame-perfect movement, exact PS1 AI, exact map scale, original voice acting, source music, motion capture, and bit-identical mechanics are not asserted.

Hub migration notes

Engine boundary: the embedded TypeScript is separated into BT (renderer bootstrap, GPU fallback, geometry submission, input, audio, local storage, fixed loop, quality) , BlackTide.LivingDock (destructibles, prop simulation, environment geometry), and BlackTide.Game (level, AI, interactions, HUD), plus App for delivery UI. No runtime dependency, CDN import, copied library file, external texture, font, worker, or WASM download is used. The browser runs the embedded classic JavaScript bundle; The embedded TypeScript is compiled into one classic-script bundle. This pass uses TypeScript 5.8.3. Vite is not present.

Work required for the requested hub: replace BT.Device, the custom GLSL/WGSL shaders, and Geometry submission with the hub's three.js r186 renderer and materials using bare package specifiers. The present custom shaders are not TSL and are a nonstandard rendering path requiring explicit migration. Replace the grenade/character and LivingDock sphere-body, hinge, and spring collision layers with hub physics where needed, initialize Rapier 0.20.0 before game start, and map collider lifecycle to the hub's body budget. The game currently uses engine vector/matrix helpers rather than importing three.js. No custom Object3D subclass, skinning system, Clock, removed TSL symbol, or postprocessing library is relied upon.

Adapt the canvas radar/HUD and DOM menus to the hub's UI, storage namespace, and input focus ownership. Share the renderer, audio context, and global listeners instead of instantiating them per game. Preserve async initialization, loading coverage, first-gesture audio unlock, and fixed-step gameplay. Scene geometry and all original audio can remain embedded or be moved into the hub asset system. Dispose GPU buffers, textures, render targets, listeners, and the audio context when removing the standalone engine. The standalone page has no router or host dependency.

Embedded audio manifest / credits

All playback resolves through the single audio-manifest JSON object in this HTML. Each entry contains embedded MP3 bytes, category, gain, loop flag, and credit. Replacing an entry's data URI and credit preserves gameplay identifiers. Music crossfades between infiltration and alert. Sound effects use the same manager and can be positioned in stereo. Assets were generated from original oscillators, filtered noise, envelopes, and a newly composed score; they contain no source-game samples.

The requested archives—The Sounds Resource and Zophar's Metal Gear Solid archive—were checked, but their assets could not be retrieved in the build environment. They are research/request references only, not sources of audio used in this file. The requested source-game placeholder-audio requirement therefore remains unmet.
